articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA — the agency literally tasked with protecting America's cyber infrastructure — left AWS GovCloud credentials sitting in a public GitHub repo like a rookie. The irony is so thick you could patch vulnerabilities with it.

articles.title: CISA Exposes Secrets, Credentials in 'Private' Repo
articles.summary: Yet another Windows zero-day trilogy drops post-Patch Tuesday because apparently Microsoft's security is like a leaky dam — plug one hole, three more spring up. YellowKey, GreenPlasma, and MiniPlasma join the hall of shame.

articles.title: Clear your calendar, Drupal user: You have a critically urgent patch to install
articles.summary: CISA's 'Private' GitHub repo was about as private as a Times Square billboard, complete with files helpfully named 'AWS-Workspace-Firefox-Passwords.csv' because subtlety is dead. America's top cyber defenders, everyone.

articles.title: The New Phishing Click: How OAuth Consent Bypasses MFA
articles.summary: DirtyDecrypt PoC is now in the wild for Linux kernel CVE-2026-31635, because nothing says 'Monday motivation' like fresh local privilege escalation exploits. Time to patch, penguins.

articles.title: Mexican government breached by solo user with Claude, 150 GB exfiltrated
articles.summary: MiniPlasma zero-day hands out SYSTEM privileges on Windows 11 like candy at Halloween, with PoC included for maximum chaos. Chaotic Eclipse lives up to their name — respect the craft, fear the implications.

articles.title: TrendAI™ Zero Day Initiative Leads Industry Remediation at Pwn2Own Berlin
articles.summary: One person with Claude AI just casually exfiltrated 150GB from the Mexican government, proving that AI democratizes pwning entire nations. The future is here and it bills monthly.

articles.title: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: Activity Through 2026-05-17, (Mon, May 18th)
articles.summary: Hackers stole Grafana's already-open-source code then demanded ransom to not release it publicly — the technical equivalent of threatening to tell everyone your secrets that are already on Wikipedia. Grafana rightfully told them to pound sand.

articles.title: Your Privacy Shouldn't Be A Corporate Decision
articles.summary: Microsoft actually took a step toward human rights accountability in tech infrastructure deals, setting a precedent that Google and Amazon are probably ignoring while counting their government contract money.

articles.title: We Updated Our Privacy Policy. Here's What Changed and Why.
articles.summary: Meta planned to launch face recognition for smart glasses during 'dynamic political times' when civil society would be 'distracted' — because nothing says ethical tech like timing privacy violations with democratic chaos.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Exchange 0-Day, npm Worm, Fake AI Repo, Cisco Exploit and More
articles.summary: ShinyHunters hit 7-Eleven for 600,000+ Salesforce records because apparently Big Gulps aren't the only thing getting supersized at convenience stores. Thank you, come again (to check if your data was stolen).
